Here's a descriptive, fictional, imaginative alternate timeline of the world where feudalism never became obsolete:

  In the year 1500, the world was a vastly different place. The Renaissance had never occurred, and the Enlightenment had never taken hold. Instead, the feudal system had continued to evolve and thrive, with lords and ladies ruling over their domains with absolute power.

  The nobility had become increasingly powerful, and the common folk lived in a state of subservience. The peasants toiled in the fields, working long hours for meager wages, while the nobles lived in luxury, feasting and drinking their way through the days.

  The monarchs, who had once been the ultimate authority, had been reduced to mere figureheads. The real power lay with the nobles, who had formed a complex web of alliances and rivalries that spanned the globe.

  In Europe, the great kingdoms of England, France, and Spain had become even more centralized, with the nobles holding sway over the monarchs. The peasants were forced to pay heavy taxes and tributes, which were used to fund the wars and conquests of the nobles.

  In Asia, the great empires of China, Japan, and India had continued to thrive, with the nobles ruling over their subjects with an iron fist. The peasants were forced to work long hours in the fields, and the nobles lived in opulence, surrounded by their concubines and eunuchs.

  In Africa, the great kingdoms of Egypt, Ethiopia, and Mali had become even more powerful, with the nobles controlling the flow of trade and commerce. The peasants were forced to pay heavy taxes and tributes, which were used to fund the wars and conquests of the nobles.

  In the Americas, the great empires of the Aztecs and Incas had continued to thrive, with the nobles ruling over their subjects with absolute power. The peasants were forced to work long hours in the fields, and the nobles lived in luxury, surrounded by their concubines and slaves.

  As the centuries passed, the feudal system continued to evolve, with new technologies and innovations being introduced to the system. The nobles began to use gunpowder and cannons to wage war, and the peasants were forced to adapt to the new ways of warfare.

  Despite the many changes, the feudal system remained largely unchanged. The nobles continued to hold power, and the peasants continued to live in a state of subservience. The world was a vastly different place, and the people lived in a state of constant fear and oppression.

  In this world, the concept of democracy and equality had never existed. The nobles were the only ones who mattered, and the peasants were nothing more than serfs, bound to the land and forced to work for the benefit of their lords.

  The world was a dark and foreboding place, where the strong preyed on the weak, and the nobles ruled with an iron fist. It was a world where the concept of freedom and justice had never existed, and the people lived in a state of constant fear and oppression.

  And yet, despite the many hardships and injustices, there were still those who dared to dream of a better world. The peasants, who toiled in the fields, whispered among themselves of a time when they would be free, when they would be equal, and when they would be able to live their lives as they saw fit.

  But for now, the feudal system remained the dominant force in the world, and the people lived in a state of constant fear and oppression. The world was a dark and foreboding place, where the strong preyed on the weak, and the nobles ruled with an iron fist.
